questions.question: Big O Notation — O(1), O(n), O(log n), O(n²)?

options.A: Big O là về memory chỉ
options.B: Big O: worst-case time/space complexity. O(1)=constant, O(log n)=binary search, O(n)=linear, O(n log n)=merge sort, O(n²)=bubble sort
options.D: Big O không quan trọng trong thực tế

questions.explanation: Big O: asymptotic upper bound. O(1): array access, hash table lookup. O(log n): binary search, balanced BST. O(n): linear scan, single pass. O(n log n): merge sort, heap sort, efficient sorts. O(n²): nested loops, bubble/insertion sort. O(2^n): recursive Fibonacci without memoization. O(n!): permutations. Drop constants: O(2n) = O(n). Drop lower terms: O(n² + n) = O(n²). Space complexity: O(1) in-place, O(n) extra space. Interview: explain your solution's complexity.

questions.question: Array vs Linked List — trade-offs?

options.A: Linked List luôn tốt hơn Array
options.B: Array: O(1) random access, O(n) insert/delete middle. Linked List: O(1) insert/delete at head/tail (với pointer), O(n) random access, extra memory for pointers
options.C: Array và Linked List giống nhau
options.D: Linked List không dùng trong thực tế

questions.explanation: Array: contiguous memory, cache-friendly, O(1) index access. Insert at middle: O(n) shift. Dynamic arrays (ArrayList/vector): amortized O(1) append. Linked List: nodes with data + next pointer (doubly: prev + next). O(1) insert at known position (với pointer to node), O(n) to find position. Use cases: Array — random access, cache performance. LinkedList — frequent insert/delete at ends (queue, deque), undo/redo, LRU cache implementation. Stack: can use both. Queue: prefer deque/LinkedList.

questions.question: Hash Table — implementation và collision handling?

options.B: Hash Table: hash(key) % size → bucket. Collision: chaining (linked list) hoặc open addressing (linear probing). Average O(1), worst O(n) khi many collisions
options.C: Hash Table không hỗ trợ strings
options.D: Hash collision không thể xảy ra

questions.explanation: Hash function: map key → index. Good hash: uniform distribution, fast compute. Collision: 2 keys → same bucket. Chaining: each bucket = linked list of (key, value). O(1) average, O(n) worst. Open addressing: Linear probing (next empty slot), Quadratic probing, Double hashing. Load factor: n/m (items/buckets). When load factor > 0.7 → resize (double) → rehash all. Java HashMap: chaining, resizes at 0.75. Python dict: open addressing. Real-world: O(1) average với good hash and reasonable load factor.

questions.question: Binary Search Tree (BST) operations và time complexity?

options.B: BST: left < root < right. Search/Insert/Delete: O(h) where h=height. Balanced BST (AVL/Red-Black): O(log n). Unbalanced/skewed: O(n)
options.D: BST và Binary Tree giống nhau

questions.explanation: BST property: all left subtree < node < all right subtree. Search: compare → go left or right recursively. Insert: search then insert at null. Delete: 3 cases — no child (remove), 1 child (replace), 2 children (find inorder successor/predecessor). Height h: balanced → h = O(log n), skewed → h = O(n). Balanced BSTs: AVL Tree (strict balance, rotations), Red-Black Tree (flexible, fewer rotations, used in Java TreeMap/TreeSet). In-order traversal → sorted sequence. Use cases: sorted data with fast search, range queries.

questions.question: Dynamic Programming — memoization vs tabulation?

options.A: DP chỉ dùng cho recursive problems
options.B: Memoization (top-down): recursive + cache. Tabulation (bottom-up): iterative, fill table. DP khi: optimal substructure + overlapping subproblems
options.C: DP luôn chậm hơn brute force
options.D: Memoization và Tabulation cho kết quả khác nhau

questions.explanation: DP conditions: (1) Optimal Substructure: optimal solution = optimal solutions of subproblems. (2) Overlapping Subproblems: same subproblems computed repeatedly. Memoization: fib(n) = memo[n] if exists else compute and store. Tabulation: dp[0]=0, dp[1]=1, dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Tabulation: no recursion stack overflow, usually faster. Classic DP: Fibonacci, Knapsack, Longest Common Subsequence, Coin Change, Matrix Chain Multiplication. Interview: identify base case, recurrence relation, state variables.

questions.question: Algorithm gives wrong answer for edge cases. Debug approach?

options.A: Try all inputs until find bug
options.B: Test edge cases explicitly: empty, single element, all same, sorted/reverse sorted, max values, negatives. Draw algorithm step by step with small input

questions.explanation: Edge case checklist: Empty input ([], null, 0). Single element. Duplicate elements. Already sorted / reverse sorted. Maximum/minimum values (overflow?). Negative numbers (if applicable). All same values. Very large input (performance). Debug technique: Trace through algorithm with small input (4-5 elements) on paper/whiteboard. Add print statements at each step. Invariant checking: assert conditions that should always be true. For arrays: check off-by-one (i < n vs i <= n). For recursion: base case correct? For DP: index order correct?

questions.question: Tìm shortest path trong graph với million nodes — thuật toán nào?

options.B: Dijkstra với priority queue O(E log V) cho weighted. A* cho heuristic (maps). Bellman-Ford O(VE) cho negative weights. SSSP vs APSP

questions.explanation: Shortest path algorithms: BFS: unweighted graph, O(V+E). Dijkstra: non-negative weights, O((V+E) log V) với min-heap. Greedy, không hoạt động với negative weights. A*: heuristic guided Dijkstra, faster cho specific destination (GPS). Bellman-Ford: negative weights OK, detect negative cycles, O(VE). Floyd-Warshall: All-Pairs Shortest Path (APSP), O(V³), cho dense graphs. Scale: Google Maps với 1B nodes → bidirectional Dijkstra + contraction hierarchies. Real-world: route optimization, network routing (BGP), social graph shortest path.
